title: Contextual Route Contracts and Page Graph Sketches
body:
Purpose:

This note collects a set of working sketches for declarative route contracts, a compact page-graph for the Console, and a prioritized backlog of implementation tasks we can use for the vNext IA refactor. Goal is to define: (1) an explicit route grammar (contracts + guards), (2) a small set of navigation primitives for the left panel and contextual flyouts, and (3) migration plan that preserves deep links and telemetry.

Context / why now:
- Growing number of Console features (rollouts, model catalog, customer environments) have created deep nesting and many one-off routes.
- Current left-panel is overloaded: a mix of personae (admin, SRE, developer) and surface area (monitoring, routing policies, model ops).
- Need an IA that supports: predictable deep linking, lightweight breadcrumbs, and conditional visibility for private/dedicated tenants.

Design principles (working):
- Compact graph: prefer a single canonical path per conceptual state (no multiple canonical URLs for same UI).
- Declarative route contracts: each route declares required context (project, org, modelId, deploymentId), optional params, and visibility rules.
- Context-first navigation: panel contents are derived from current route context (not the other way around).
- Graceful fallbacks: if required context absent, show transient chooser layer (not 404).
- Minimal mutation on legacy deep-links: automatic redirect rules for known old patterns.

High-level route primitives (vocab):
- Root: /console (static base, sets app chrome)
- Workspace scope: /console/org/:orgId[/project/:projectId] (scoping root)
- Surface: /console/:scope/:surface (surface = models | deployments | routes | metrics | settings)
- Resource: /console/:scope/:surface/:resourceId[/subview] (resource-level)
- Modal/Transient: ?modal=... or /console/_modal/:modalId (used for create/edit flows)
- QueryContexts: ?qctx=embedding:small (lightweight filters, not scoping)

Example route contracts (declarative examples, written informally):
- Models list:
  path: /console/org/:orgId/models
  required: [orgId]
  optional: [projectId, qctx]
  visibility: all
  telemetry: route(models:list)

- Model detail (stable canonical):
  path: /console/org/:orgId/models/:modelId
  required: [orgId, modelId]
  optional: [version, subview]    # version pins UI to model version panel
  guards: if model.private && !user.inOrg -> redirect /console/unauthorized
  fallbacks: if modelId missing -> open model-chooser modal (/_modal/model-chooser)

Page graph sketch (ASCII):

/console
  ├─ /org/:orgId
  │   ├─ /models
  │   │   ├─ /:modelId
  │   │   │   ├─ /versions/:versionId
  │   │   │   └─ ?modal=deploy -> transient deploy flow
  │   ├─ /deployments
  │   │   ├─ /:deploymentId
  │   │   └─ /events
  │   ├─ /routes
  │   └─ /metrics
  ├─ /settings
  └─ /help (static)

Notes on left-panel behavior (primitive set):
- Primary group: Workspace selector (org + project) at the top. This is not a nav target; it sets scope for the rest.
- Secondary groups: Surface switcher (Models, Deployments, Routes, Metrics, Optimize, Settings). These map to /console/:scope/:surface.
- Tertiary: Context list (when on a surface that lists resources) shows resource shortcards and quick-actions. Selecting resource updates URL (canonical).
- Compact mode: On narrow screens or when user toggles compact-left-panel, group labels collapse into icons and resource list becomes a flyout.

Panel stacking semantics (wireframe notes):
- Stack model: base page -> resource panel -> subview (right-side panel) -> transient modal.
- Panels are URL-addressable: opening a side panel should push URL state (so back button closes).
- Back/forward behavior must be linear and reflect user-perceivable stack. Avoid URL permutations that produce same UI but different URL orderings.

Routing decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Use query params for ephemeral filters vs path params for canonical identity. Decision: identity -> path, filters -> query.
- Fold functional areas (optimize, rollout) into surfaces vs separate top-level items. Decision: group under surfaces to reduce primary nav cardinality and keep deep links concise.
- Modal URLs vs query flags. Decision: modal micro-route (/_modal/...) because some modals need to be bookmarkable (e.g., persisted walkthrough).

Edge cases and unresolved items:
- Multi-org users: how to show org switch without losing transient panel state? Proposed: persist transient panel state scoped to org; switching org will reset panels but prompt to "preserve" when compatible states exist.
- Back-compat redirects: we need a middleware to handle legacy patterns (/console/models?m=123 -> /console/org/:orgId/models/123). Need a mapping table (see linked Jira PROD-4890).
- Deeply nested resource searches: search results should be able to open resource panels without changing outer scope accidentally. Flag: open-in-panel vs navigate-to-resource.
- Access control visibility: some surfaces should be hidden entirely for orgs with limited feature sets (dedicated/private). Need a visibility registry keyed by org feature flags.

Concrete implementation backlog (prioritized):
1) Route contract spec + canonicalizer middleware (2 sprints) - produce canonical -> current mapping for legacy links, enforce single canonical path per resource. (Owner: Marco)
2) Left-panel primitives and compact mode (1 sprint) - implement workspace selector + surface switcher + compact toggle. (Owner: Lina)
3) Panel stack URL plumbing (2 sprints) - ensure open/close maps to history entries consistently. (Owner: Samir)
4) Visibility registry + guard middleware (1 sprint) - hide surfaces based on org features.
5) Redirect mapping for top 20 legacy deep links (1 sprint) - use telemetry to identify most used outdated links.
6) Docs + runbook for deep link migration (0.5 sprint)

Telemetry and rollout strategy:
- Instrument route canonicalization counts: how often legacy -> canonical redirect occurs.
- Gate migration: enable redirect-only mode first (log but don't rewrite links), then gradually enable hard redirects after 2 weeks with low error rate.
- A/B test compact-left-panel: 50% users for 2 weeks then evaluate task completion for "open deployment details" flow.

Open questions to resolve in next sync (owners listed):
- Should we include projectId in canonical model URLs when project-scoped models arrive? (Aisha to prototype impact)
- Transient state persistence across org-switch: preserve or blow away? (Product decision)
- Do we introduce named anchors for telemetry-friendly micro-actions (e.g., /.../models/123#open-logs)? (SRE implications)

Next steps (short):
- Share this doc with Eng-Platform and SRE for feedback (Marco: please route).
- Prototype a small subtree (models -> model detail -> versions) as a feature branch showing URL transitions and history behavior.
- Schedule 30m sync w/ design and infra to align on middleware approach (next Tue).

Appendix: quick sketch of a canonical redirect rule (informal):
- match: /console/models?m=:id -> resolve orgId via lookup -> redirect 302 -> /console/org/:orgId/models/:id

Notes-to-self (rough):
- Keep breadcrumbs minimal: [Org] > [Surface] > [Resource].
- Avoid showing project selector inside resource header; prefer persistent header area under chrome.
- Add a small test harness to simulate back/forward stack with panels to catch regressions.
summary: Working set of route contracts, a compact page graph, left-panel primitives, panel stacking semantics, prioritized backlog and migration/telemetry plan for Console IA refactor.
